subject.title: Preserve aborted sessions across restart opt-in

question: Should OpenClaw accept a new `session.restartContinuation` config contract for preserving interrupted `killed` or `timeout` main-session ids, now that current main already reuses successful `done` rows without a config knob?
rationale: The branch is no longer proving a current-main gap for `done` rows, and the remaining unique behavior would deliberately relax current interrupted-session rotation semantics behind a new config surface.

options.title: Retarget And Sponsor The Opt-In
options.body: Keep the PR open only if maintainers want this config contract, then require the branch to prove `killed`/`timeout` restart continuation on current main.

options.title: Close As Covered Enough By Main
options.body: Close this PR if the merged `done`-session reuse fix covers the practical lossless-claw quarantine path and interrupted-state preservation should stay guarded.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Restart Recovery
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open but redirect this PR toward the broader graceful-restart design instead of adding a narrow session config knob.

recommendation.title: Retarget And Sponsor The Opt-In
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open only if maintainers want this config contract, then require the branch to prove `killed`/`timeout` restart continuation on current main.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original transcript reconciliation behavior and are the clearest routing owner for changing the guard's session-state semantics.
